---
title: "Installation and running"
---

This page covers building VILMA2, testing the build, and running a forced
simulation. The build is driven by **configme** (one source of machine and
compiler settings) and runs are staged by **runme** (single simulations and
ensembles, locally or on SLURM). The model is built and tested on three
machines: a MacBook (gfortran), the AWI cluster albedo (ifx) and the DKRZ
cluster levante (ifx). Production runs are currently made on albedo.

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Provides | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **[fesm-utils](https://github.com/fesmc/fesm-utils)**, branch `phase0-kryos` | FFTW, SHTns, the `fesmutils` helper library (precision, ncio, namelists) and the `coords` module used by the remapper | cloned and built by configme |
| **netCDF** (C and Fortran) | input, output and restart files | system package (Homebrew, environment modules, apt) |
| **configme**, **runme** | Makefile generation; run staging | [fesmc/configme](https://github.com/fesmc/configme), [fesmc/runme](https://github.com/fesmc/runme) (`pip install`) |

The fesm-utils branch is pinned in `.configme/manifest.toml`, so a checkout
records the ref it needs. VILMA2 needs the `coords` routine
`grid_init_gaussian`, which is in `phase0-kryos` but not yet in the fesm-utils
`dev` branch: `src/vilma_remap.f90` does not compile against `dev` v1.4. The
pin returns to `dev` once `phase0-kryos` is merged there.

## Install

`configme install vilma2` clones fesm-utils into the checkout, builds its
serial and OpenMP variants (FFTW, SHTns, LIS and libfesmutils; about 10
minutes), and writes the top-level `Makefile` from `config/Makefile` and the
machine and compiler fragments. `configme show <machine>` prints a fragment,
`configme status` reports what is present and what is pending, and
`configme config vilma2` regenerates the Makefile of an existing checkout
without cloning. To reuse an existing fesm-utils checkout instead of cloning
one, add `--link fesm-utils=/abs/path/to/fesm-utils`.

The optimization flags differ by machine. The macbook fragment is the
repository's own (`.configme/machines/macbook.mk`): gfortran
`-O3 -mcpu=native -funroll-loops -ffast-math`. The clusters use configme's
fragments: ifx `-Ofast -march=znver2 -traceback` on albedo (AMD EPYC 7702) and
`-Ofast -march=znver3 -traceback` on levante (AMD EPYC 7763). The benchmark
numbers in these pages were measured with the albedo build.

### MacBook (gfortran)

```bash
brew install gcc netcdf netcdf-fortran
pip install git+https://github.com/fesmc/configme.git git+https://github.com/fesmc/runme.git
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/vilma2.git && cd vilma2
configme install vilma2 -m macbook -c gfortran
make -j 8 vilma
make check
```

### AWI albedo (ifx)

The system git has been removed from the login nodes, so load the git module
first. The Intel compiler and netCDF modules must be loaded before configme
runs, so that it finds `nf-config`.

```bash
module load git intel-oneapi-compilers netcdf-c netcdf-fortran
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/vilma2.git && cd vilma2
configme install vilma2 -m awi_albedo -c ifx
make openmp=1 -j 8 vilma            # on the login node, at most -j 8
```

Compile on the login node and run the tests and the model through SLURM (see
[Testing the build](#testing-the-build)). The compute nodes have no git. The
build does not need it: the version string compiled into the model comes from
`git describe` and falls back to `"unknown"` where git is missing.

### DKRZ levante (ifx)

```bash
module load git intel-oneapi-compilers netcdf-c netcdf-fortran
git clone git@github.com:fesmc/vilma2.git && cd vilma2
configme install vilma2 -m dkrz_levante -c ifx
make openmp=1 -j 8 vilma
```

The build on levante has been verified (ifx 2023.2, netCDF-Fortran 4.6.2). No
runs have been made there yet.

## Build

```bash
make vilma        # -> bin/vilma.x        (standalone forced-run driver)
make vilma_mkref  # -> bin/vilma_mkref.x  (build a Gauss-grid reference state)
make vilma_remap  # -> bin/vilma_remap.x  (offline lon-lat -> Gauss remap)
make vilma-static # -> libvilma/include/libvilma.a and the .mod files
make bench_visc3d # -> bin/bench_visc3d.x (lateral-viscosity benchmark driver)
```

`make vilma-static` is the library that a host (kryos, CLIMBER-X) links:
objects, `.mod` files and `libvilma.a` are written to `libvilma/include/`, and
the archive is rebuilt only when an object changes. `openmp=0` and `openmp=1`
share that directory. Changing the setting rebuilds every object, and the host
must use the matching fesm-utils variant (`include-serial` or `include-omp`).

Build switches: `debug = 0|1|2` (optimized, checks, profile), `openmp = 0|1`
(**default 1**) and `vilma_v1 = 0|1` (the optional VILMA1 backend, see
[`doc/vilma-v1-backend.md`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/doc/vilma-v1-backend.md)).
The threaded degree loop is what makes production resolutions fast (see
[Solver](discretization/solver.qmd)). After switching to another fesm-utils
checkout, run `make clean`: objects compiled against the old module files can
fail to rebuild.

## Testing the build

```bash
make check                  # the test suite: about 50 tests, ~2 min
make openmp=1 check-slow    # full-resolution benchmarks and order tests, ~10 min on 32 threads
```

Both targets run every test, print a summary that names the failing tests, and
exit with a non-zero status if any failed. `check-slow` runs the four
sea-level benchmark cases, the low-viscosity-zone benchmark, the off-pole
rotational-invariance test at $\ell_\max = 128$ and three convergence-order
tests (strain–memory coupling, sea-level–memory coupling, adaptive step
control). It raises the stack limit itself. Setting `VILMA_BENCH_DUMP` to a
directory makes the benchmark tests write their comparison tables there (see
[Benchmarks](benchmarks/index.qmd#dumping-the-comparison-data)).

On albedo, run both suites in a job, with the executables built beforehand on
the login node (`make openmp=1 -j 8 check` builds them and then runs the tests;
interrupt it once the build is done, or build the targets listed in `TESTS` and
`SLOW` in `config/Makefile_vilma.mk`). A minimal job script:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=<project> --partition=smp --qos=12h --time=01:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=32 --mem=60G
source ~/.bash_profile
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK
make openmp=1 check; make openmp=1 check-slow
```

**Known state.** With ifx `-Ofast` on albedo, all 49 tests of `make check` and
all 9 runs of `make check-slow` pass, with the default stack settings. A GitHub workflow builds the model
with gfortran on Ubuntu and runs `make check` on every push and pull request to
`main`.

## Configuration: `&vilma` and `&ctl`

A run configuration has two namelist groups:

- **`&vilma`**: the model's physics and numerics. This is the record a host
  model fills in memory.
- **`&ctl`**: the standalone run itself: forcing, reference and output files,
  the time window, `i_eq`, online remapping and the restart path. A host model
  never reads it.

The complete, documented `&vilma` defaults are in
[`input/vilma_defaults.nml`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/input/vilma_defaults.nml)
and are loaded automatically. A run configuration such as
[`vilma.nml`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/vilma.nml) (the
default) or
[`examples/deglac_lgm.nml`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/examples/deglac_lgm.nml)
carries the full `&ctl` group plus only the `&vilma` parameters it overrides
(the yelmo `defaults_file` convention). A `&vilma` key the defaults file does
not declare, such as a typo or a renamed parameter, stops the run:

```bash
./bin/vilma.x examples/deglac_lgm.nml    # default: vilma.nml
./bin/vilma.x run.nml my_defaults.nml    # optional second argument: another defaults file
```

`vilma_remap.x` and `vilma_mkref.x` take the same optional second argument;
they too need the full `&ctl` group.

A few conventions worth knowing:

- **Time fields** (`dt_*`, `time_*`, `equil_time_max`) are given in **years**
  in the namelist and converted to SI seconds on load; `equil_rate_tol` is in
  m/yr. Everything else is SI. A host that fills `se%par` in memory sets the
  time fields in seconds.
- **Earth structure** is chosen by `earth`: a named built-in (`"M3-L70-V01"`,
  or `"PREM"`, which fills $\rho,\mu$ from shell averages of incompressible PREM
  on the given layer geometry) or `"custom"` to assemble from the surface-first
  layer arrays. The radial mesh follows the depth of each element (see
  [Radial finite elements](discretization/radial-fe.qmd)).
- **Response solver** is chosen by `earth_response`: `"ve"` (full viscoelastic,
  default), `"elastic"`, or `"null"`.
- **Memory scheme** is chosen by `scheme`: `"fe"` (explicit, default) or
  `"trap"` (2nd-order, adaptive); see
  [Rheology](physics/rheology.qmd#memory-time-schemes).
- **Degree-1 frame** is chosen by `deg1_frame`: `"cm"` (default) or `"cf"`; see
  [Sea-level equation](physics/sea-level.qmd#reference-frame-and-degree-1).
- **Reference state** is chosen by `i_eq` (`&ctl`). Relative sea level is
  measured against this relaxed reference.
  - `0`: the state at the start of the run window is the equilibrium: the
    forcing's ice at that slice and the bed `name_z_bed_start`, read from
    `file_forcing` (lon, lat, time) or, with `remap_input = .false.`, from
    the 2-D `file_ref`.
  - `1` (default): a present-day reference from `z_bed_ref_file` and
    `h_ice_ref_file`, so that rsl is about zero at the present day.
  - `2`: an equilibrium state read from `z_bed_eq_file` and `h_ice_eq_file`
    (e.g. an LGM state).
  - `3`: the present-day reference bed plus the rsl field of
    `rsl_restart_file`.

  The variable names in these files are set by `name_z_bed_ref`,
  `name_h_ice_ref` and `name_rsl`.
- **Spin-up** is controlled by `equil_time_max`, `equil_rate_tol` (the memory
  is relaxed under the start-of-run load until the bed is stationary) and
  `pre_spinup_1d` (a cheap 1-D pre-equilibration first); see
  [Spin-up](discretization/time-stepping.qmd#spin-up).
- **3-D viscosity** is enabled with `l_visc_3d = .true.` and a lateral
  `log10(eta)` field (`visc_3d_file`). With `visc_3d_structure = n` (n ≥ 1) the
  file is in the FesmData layout (`log10_visc` on `lon`, `lat`, `depth`,
  `structure`) and structure `n` is read. The default is the FesmData product
  `fesmdata/Global/GLOBAL-T170/GLOBAL-T170_SolidEarth-Bagge2021.nc`
  (@Bagge2021; structure 6, `v_1.0_s16`). The path is relative to the run
  folder, which needs a `fesmdata` link to the FesmData store (on levante
  `/work/ba1442/fesmdata`). The model does not ship a viscosity file. The field
  can be shifted by `f_visc_sd` standard deviations (σ from the variable
  `name_visc_sd`, or `f_visc_rel` |log10 η|) and by region and depth with
  `visc_shift_file`. It is then clamped to
  `visc_log10_min`–`visc_log10_max`, and `visc_3d_lid_depth` and
  `visc_3d_lid_log10max` make its top effectively elastic. `visc_3d_tol` sets
  which elements are treated as genuinely 3-D. The order of these steps is given
  in [Rheology](physics/rheology.qmd#visc3d-input).
- **Toroidal flow** (`l_toroidal`) is **on by default**: with lateral
  viscosity it changes local relative sea level near former ice sheets by up
  to about 90 m in a deglaciation, though global means only by centimetres.
  `l_toroidal = .false.` makes such runs 1.5–1.8 times faster, for quick runs
  that do not depend on local sea level (see
  [Toroidal flow](physics/toroidal.qmd)).
- **Rotational feedback** (`l_rotation`) is **on by default** for real-Earth runs.
  Set `l_rotation = .false.` for the non-rotating community benchmarks. The
  secular Love number in the Liouville equation defaults to the model's own
  fluid limit; `rotation_k_s` (> 0) prescribes it and `rotation_c_minus_a` sets
  C − A (default 2.63e35 kg m²).
- **Forcing.** The ice-thickness forcing is a lon-lat field (global or
  regional) on a time axis in years (`kyr` is converted; ages and other units
  stop the run) that must be strictly ascending. The ice ramps linearly between
  slices. The axes `name_lon`, `name_lat` are cell centres; longitudes must
  ascend, latitudes may ascend or descend. A regional source is remapped with
  its mass conserved and no ice outside it. Missing, non-finite or
  out-of-range values stop the run (put zero where there is no ice).
  The remap weights are cached in `maps/` in the working directory, keyed by
  the grid dimensions and a hash of the axis values.
- **Output.** `file_out` receives the diagnostic surface fields at every
  forcing slice, including the convergence of the sea-level solve
  (`sle_resid`, the worst relative inner residual of the interval, and
  `sle_n_cap`, the number of solves that ended at an iteration cap; the model
  also warns once per interval when a cap is hit) and the uplift rate
  `dz_bed_rate` [m/yr], the change of the bed `dz_bed` over the interval
  that ends at the slice divided by its length: the mean rate of that
  interval, so a present-day slice after a short interval (a century, say)
  gives the rate a GNSS station measures (in the frame of `deg1_frame`). The folder of `file_out` is
  created if needed. `file_hor` (optional) receives the horizontal surface
  displacement.
  The variables and their output precision are listed in
  [`input/vilma-variables.md`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/input/vilma-variables.md).
  Diagnostics are rounded to that precision. `write_lossless = .true.`
  (`&ctl`) writes them lossless, as needed for bit-for-bit comparisons. Restart
  files are always lossless.
- **Restart.** The driver writes the full model state to
  `spinup/vilma_restart.nc` after the spin-up and to `final/vilma_restart.nc`
  at the end of the run, in the run directory. `restart_in_file` (`&ctl`)
  resumes from such a file: the model is initialized at the reference and the
  saved state is restored, so a resumed run continues the original one bit for
  bit. If a spin-up is enabled, it then runs from the restored state. A
  restart from a lower degree is padded: its memory fills the shared low
  degrees and the higher degrees start at zero (not bit for bit).
  The run resumes at the restart's time: a `time_init` that selects another
  start stops it, unless `restart_time_reset = .true.` (`&ctl`), which takes the
  restart as the state at the start of the window. A restart from another
  radial mesh is refused. A restart from another viscosity (radial profile or
  3-D field, both stamped in the file) is refused unless
  `restart_other_visc = .true.` (`&ctl`), which uses its memory as a seed. Restarts of the default
  PREM model written before the depth-based mesh rule (220 instead of 219
  elements) are therefore refused; `mesh_depth = 80e3, 670e3` rebuilds the old
  mesh exactly. What the restart carries and what is checked on read is
  described in
  [Time stepping](discretization/time-stepping.qmd#memory-storage-and-restart).
- **Backend** is chosen by `solver`: `"v2"` (this model, default) or `"v1"`,
  the VILMA1 library behind the same driver, forcing and output for
  like-for-like comparison (requires a build with `vilma_v1=1`).

### Parameter reference

Every `&vilma` parameter and its default is documented in
[`input/vilma_defaults.nml`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/input/vilma_defaults.nml),
and every `&ctl` parameter in `src/vilma_control.f90`. The physics and
numerics pages describe most of them in context. The remaining ones are:

| Group | Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `&vilma` grid | `lmax` | maximum spherical-harmonic degree (64 in the defaults file; the in-memory record has none, so a host must set it) |
| | `nlat`, `nphi` | Gauss latitudes and longitudes; 0 gives the de-aliased defaults $2\ell_\max + 2$ and $4\ell_\max$ |
| | `mmax`, `mres` | maximum order (< 0: `lmax`) and order stride |
| | `eps_polar` | SHTns polar-optimization threshold (< 0: library default) |
| `&vilma` custom earth (`earth = "custom"` or `"PREM"`) | `n_layer`, `r_earth`, `r_core` | number of layers (surface first), surface and core radius [m] |
| | `r_bot`, `r_top` | inner and outer radius of each layer [m] |
| | `rho`, `mu`, `eta` | density, shear modulus and viscosity of each layer (`rho`, `mu` filled from PREM for `"PREM"`) |
| | `rheology` | per layer: 0 elastic, 1 Maxwell, 2 fluid |
| `&vilma` VILMA1 backend (`solver = "v1"` only) | `vilma_v1_jmax`, `vilma_v1_nsub` | VILMA1 degree and sub-steps per coupling interval |
| | `vilma_v1_input_dir`, `vilma_v1_out_dir`, `vilma_v1_grid_file` | VILMA1 input directory, scratch directory and grid |
| | `vilma_v1_visc_1d_file`, `vilma_v1_visc_3d_file`, `vilma_v1_l_prem` | VILMA1 viscosity files and earth-structure choice |
| `&ctl` forcing | `file_forcing`, `name_h_ice`, `name_time` | ice-thickness forcing (lon, lat, time [yr]) and its variable names |
| | `name_lon`, `name_lat` | longitude and latitude axes of every 2-D input file [deg], in both modes; with `remap_input = .false.` they must be the Gauss grid's (longitudes from 0) |
| | `time_init`, `time_end` | run window [yr]; default the first and the last forcing slice |
| | `remap_input` | `.true.` (default): remap lon-lat input online; `.false.`: input already on the Gauss grid |
| `&ctl` start-slice bed (`i_eq = 0`) | `name_z_bed_start`, `file_ref` | bed variable, read from `file_forcing` (lon, lat, time), or from the 2-D Gauss-grid `file_ref` with `remap_input = .false.` |
| `&ctl` restart | `restart_in_file`, `restart_time_reset`, `restart_other_visc` | see above |
| `&ctl` output | `file_out`, `file_hor`, `write_lossless` | see above |

## The drivers

| Executable | Role |
|---|---|
| `bin/vilma.x` | reads a reference state and an ice-thickness forcing `h_ice(lon,lat,time)`, marches the model across the forcing (online lon-lat → Gauss remap by default), and writes the diagnostic surface fields (`rsl`, `z_bed`, `h_ice`, ocean function) to `file_out`, and optionally the horizontal surface displacement to `file_hor` |
| `bin/vilma_mkref.x` | generates the canonical Gauss-grid present-day reference (e.g. RTopo) used by `i_eq = 1`; other resolutions remap it online (cached in `maps/`) |
| `bin/vilma_remap.x` | offline conservative lon-lat → Gauss remap, to preprocess a forcing onto the model grid (`remap_input = .false.`) |

A complete worked configuration, an LGM to present-day deglaciation, is in
[`examples/deglac_lgm.nml`](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/examples/deglac_lgm.nml).

## Running with runme

`runme` stages a clean run directory (linking in `data` and `input`, copying the
namelist, recording the parameters), then runs or submits it. The executable
aliases match the drivers: `main` → `vilma.x`, `mkref` → `vilma_mkref.x`,
`remap` → `vilma_remap.x`, `visc3d` → `bench_visc3d.x`.

```bash
# single local run, 8 OpenMP threads, overriding a few parameters
runme -o runs/deglac -e main --omp 8 -r \
      -p vilma.lmax=128 vilma.earth_response=ve ctl.file_out=out.nc
```

How a run is launched is set by two flags:

- `-r` runs the executable;
- `-s` prepares a SLURM submit script (and submits it, with `-r`);
- `-s -r` prepares **and** submits on HPC; `-s` alone stages the script to
  inspect; omitting both stages the run directory only.

A comma list, range, or distribution in `-p` turns a parameter into an
**ensemble dimension** (`-p vilma.lmax=64,128`), with `-a` naming the member
directories from their parameter values.

SLURM settings live in `.runme/config.toml`, which is not tracked. Copy
`.runme/config.default.toml` or run `runme config init`, then set the cluster
(`hpc`, a key of `runme queues --all`) and the account; `runme info` shows what
runme reads. On albedo:

```toml
hpc     = "awi_albedo"
account = "<project>"        # e.g. the p_forclima project account
omp     = 32
```

```bash
runme -o runs/deglac_lgm -e main -n examples/deglac_lgm.nml --omp 32 \
      -q 12h -w 06:00:00 -s -r -p vilma.lmax=128
```

On levante (`hpc = "dkrz_levante"`, `account = "<project>"`):

```bash
runme -o runs/deglac_lgm -e main -n examples/deglac_lgm.nml --omp 64 \
      -q compute -w 06:00:00 -s -r -p vilma.lmax=128
```

## Embedding in a host model

The CLIMBER-X coupling path uses the same code behind a single
`use vilma`. The contract is narrow: the host passes **ice thickness** in and
receives **relative sea level** and **bedrock** out, on its own grid. The model
owns its Gauss grid and the host↔Gauss remap (built from the parameter record),
and keeps all spherical-harmonic work inside (see
[Implementation](implementation.qmd)):

```fortran
use vilma
type(solid_earth) :: se
call vilma_par_load(se%par, "vilma.nml", defaults_file=DEFAULTS_FILE)  ! configuration lives in se%par
call solid_earth_init(se, z_bed_eq, h_ice_eq, grid=host_grid, time=t0)  ! Gauss grid + remap; clock at t0 [yr]
call solid_earth_spinup(se, h_ice_lgm)                ! optional LGM-memory spin-up (holds the clock)
do
   call solid_earth_update(se, h_ice, dt_yr)          ! advance dt_yr [years]
   ! ... read se%rsl, se%z_bed, se%dz_bed, se%dz_ss, se%C on the host grid ...
   ! ... rsl = se%dz_ss - se%dz_bed: the sea-surface change N + dphi and the bed change u ...
   ! ... se%dz_bed_rate = (u(t) - u(t - dt_yr))/dt_yr [m/yr]: the uplift rate over the interval ...
end do
call solid_earth_finalize(se)                         ! frees the grid too
```

`use vilma` is the only module a host needs: it exports the parameter record,
`solid_earth` and its life cycle, the checks and the restart routines, and
nothing internal. `h_ice` is the whole ice column; the model applies its own
flotation rule to it. The model keeps its own clock: `solid_earth_init` sets it
(`time`, default 0), each update advances it, and `solid_earth_set_time`
relabels it without changing the state. A host never writes `se%time`. A
negative `dt_yr` stops the run; `dt_yr = 0` re-solves the surface fields under
the ice passed in.

`grid` (a coords lon-lat grid) is optional: omit it when the fields are already
on the model's Gauss grid in the SHTns layout (rows north first). A `grid` that
is the Gauss grid passes the fields through exactly, in its own row order
(latitude ascending, as coords builds it, or descending). Any other global grid
is remapped; a regional grid is refused. The host-grid fields are always in the
order the host supplied; `se%gg` is the internal Gauss-grid state. The full
prognostic state is persisted on restart (`vilma_restart_write`,
`vilma_restart_read`), so a coupled run resumes bit for bit; the host-grid
outputs are re-derived on read.

`vilma_par_load` overlays the user file on `defaults_file`; without it the
user file must hold every `&vilma` parameter. A host that fills `se%par` in
memory instead starts from the in-code defaults, which leave `lmax` unset.
The rest of the interface:

| Procedure | Use |
|---|---|
| `solid_earth_check_solver(par)` | validate `solver` (and that a `"v1"` build has VILMA1) before any work |
| `solid_earth_set_time(se, time)` | relabel the clock [yr] without changing the state |
| `solid_earth_sync_host(se)` | refresh the host-grid outputs from the Gauss-grid state |
| `solid_earth_enable_visc_3d(se, sht)` | switch to the 3-D memory advance, keeping the memory (e.g. after a 1-D spin-up); init calls it when `l_visc_3d` is on |
| `solid_earth_host_check(w, I_g, C, F, msg, tol)` | admissibility of host-resolved terms (`tol` default 1e-9) |
| `vilma_restart_write(se, time, filename, folder, init)` | write the full state; defaults `./vilma_restart.nc`, `init = .false.` appends a snapshot |
| `vilma_restart_read(se, filename, time, other_visc)` | restore the state at `time` (default the last snapshot) into an initialized `se` |
| `vilma_restart_time(filename)` | time [yr] of the last snapshot |
| `vilma_restart_compatible(se, filename, msg, other_visc)` | the checks `vilma_restart_read` applies, without reading |
| `vilma_write_step`, `vilma_write_horizontal` | diagnostic output, as the standalone driver writes it |
| `vilma_io_set_table(filename)` | path of the variable table (default `input/vilma-variables.md`) |
| `vilma_version` | the model version string |

Two files are read relative to the working directory: the variable table
`input/vilma-variables.md`, which every output and restart write uses (set
another path with `vilma_io_set_table`), and the remap-weight cache `maps/`,
keyed by the grid dimensions and a hash of the axis values.

### Host-resolved terms (optional)

A host that resolves the ice margin on its own grid, inside regions of weight
$w$, can pass on that grid, per unit cell area, the grounded-ice column
$I_g = w H f_g$, the ocean fraction $C = w (1 - f_g)$ and the flooded-area fill
$F = w \zeta^{(0)} (C - C_\text{ref})$:

```fortran
call solid_earth_init(se, z_bed_eq, h_ice_eq, grid, w=w, I_g=I_g, C=C)    ! reference terms
call solid_earth_spinup(se, h_ice_lgm, w, I_g, C, F)                      ! held over every pass
call solid_earth_update(se, h_ice, dt_yr, w, I_g, C, F)                   ! ramped like the ice
ok = solid_earth_host_check(w, I_g, C, F, msg)                            ! admissibility
```

Inside $w$ the sea-level solve uses these terms. On $1 - w$ it applies its own
flotation and coastline rule, and `h_ice`, `h_ice_eq` are the ice of that part
(cells with $w = 1$ ignore them). The terms are all or none and fixed for the
run. They cannot be combined with `solver = "v1"` or `sle_fixed_ocean`, and $F$ enters only through the sub-grid term (`sle_subgrid`).
Without them, or with $w \equiv 0$, a run is bit-identical to one without. The
terms are part of the restart. Details are in the
[sea-level equation](physics/sea-level.qmd) page and in
[`doc/design.md` §15](https://github.com/fesmc/vilma2/blob/main/doc/design.md).
